summary: Reviewers mostly praise Cirque Colors' formula, especially its jellies and magnetics, as smooth, easy to apply and self-leveling, and many say it wears well. The main downsides are sheer jellies that can take three or four coats and repeated complaints that website swatches don't match the real color. A few found it streaky or quick to chip.

Most reviewers say Dazzle Dry dries in about five minutes without a lamp and lasts a week or two, often longer than gel or regular polish. The main complaints are price and, for some, chipping or free-edge wear within a few days even after following the full system. Several switching from gel say their nails got healthier, though a few had peeling.

Many reviewers credit Essie Gel Couture Top Coat with a plump, glossy finish and manicures that last about a week, and many find it dries reasonably fast. The most common complaint is shrinkage at the tips or cuticle, often worse as the bottle ages. Some see the shine fade after a few days, and several say it can disperse magnetic polish.

Most reviewers love Essie Gel Setter for a thick, plump, gel-like shine, and many find it dries fairly fast despite not being sold as quick-dry. Shrinkage is the most frequent complaint, though plenty never get it and capping the tips helps. Some find it gets thick or gloopy later in the bottle, and several like it over magnetic polish.

Most reviewers get one to three weeks from Glamnetic press-ons, often crediting strong glue and careful prep. Some had nails pop off, crack or chip within a day or a few days. Several found removal slow and difficult, and a few say the sets are too curved or don't fit their nail beds.

Many reviewers get a week or more of wear from Holo Taco and praise its opaque, often one-coat cremes. A thick formula is the most common complaint, though a few like it for less cuticle flooding, and some say it chips within a day or a few days. Opinions also split by finish, with some loving the glitters and holos but not the cremes.

Many reviewers like ILNP's formulas and value and get about a week of wear, though some say it chips within days. The biggest complaint is bottles thickening over months and needing thinner, and many find it fairly sheer, often needing three coats. Several also dislike the thin stock brush.

Most reviewers say Mooncat wears longer than other brands, commonly a week or more without chips. The main complaint is a thick formula that can need thinner, and some find it chips quickly, is overpriced or varies from shade to shade. Several praise the brushes and easy application.

Most reviewers find Mooncat Speed Demon dries fast and hard with a plump, glossy finish, and several report little or no shrinkage. The dominant complaint is that it turns thick and stringy, often around halfway through the bottle, and needs frequent thinner. Some also find it pricey for a top coat.

Most reviewers rely on Sally Hansen Insta-Dri for fast drying at a low price, and many say it doesn't shrink their polish. The main complaint is chipping or cracking, sometimes within a day, and some find it less glossy than pricier top coats. Results over magnetic polish are mixed, and a few report bubbles.

Seche Vite is loved for drying within minutes with a deep, glossy finish, and many reviewers get a week or more of wear at a low price. The common downsides are shrinkage and pulling back at the tips, a strong smell, and a formula that turns gloopy partway down the bottle. It works best applied over still-wet polish with the tips capped, and some find it lifts or shrinks regardless.

Reviews of OPI Nail Lacquer are split. Fans find the cremes and reds reliable and glossy, and some get a week or more of wear. The most common complaint is streaky, uneven application in lighter shades, notably Bubble Bath, followed by quick chipping, a thick or gloopy formula and slow drying. Many also dislike the brush, and quality seems to vary by shade.

Essie Nail Polish gets a mixed response. Some find it easy to apply with a nice brush, glossy, and lasting a week or more, and the creme shades are often praised. The biggest complaint is chipping, with a number of reviewers saying it chips within days or fails to dry on them. Pale and sheer shades can be streaky, and some bottles turn thick or gloopy. Results seem to depend on the person and the shade.

Sally Hansen Insta-Dri is mainly praised for drying very fast, often in one thin coat, at a good price. The main complaint is a formula that turns thick and gloopy, or dries out in the bottle, and the wide brush bothers some. Wear is mixed, with some getting a week or more and others seeing chips within days. It suits quick manicures applied in thin coats.

Sally Hansen Miracle Gel is mostly liked for lasting well, often a week or more without a UV lamp, with a glossy finish, easy application and fairly quick drying. Downsides include chipping or peeling for some, a thick formula, and a few shades that are sheer or need several coats. A handful report it never fully dries. It works best in thin coats with its matching top coat.

Seche Vive Instant Gel Effect Top Coat is liked for drying quickly, a plump gel-like shine and a week or so of wear. Many say it shrinks less than Seche Vite, though a few still see shrinkage. The main downsides are a strong smell from the fumes, thickening that needs thinner, and disturbing magnetic polishes. A few reported lifting or a reaction to its ingredients.

ORLY Nail Lacquer is well liked for an easy-to-apply formula, a comfortable paddle brush and big bottles, with cremes singled out and many saying it wears well. The downsides are mostly from a minority: chipping or flaking for some, a thin or sheer formula in lighter colors needing extra coats, and a few cases of thick formula or strong smell. Many prefer it to OPI.

OPI Nail Envy Nail Strengthener is credited by most reviewers with strengthening weak, thin or peeling nails, often used as a base coat. The main complaint is that for some it made nails peel, turn brittle or flimsy, with several blaming a newer formula. Results seem to vary by person, and a few find it pricey. It suits weak or peeling nails, with a trial period to see how nails respond.

Olive & June Nail Polish divides reviewers. Fans get a week or more without chipping, with a glossy, gel-like look and a brush many love. Others find it chips within days, streaky in lighter shades, or thick and gloopy, and some say it dries slowly. Pastels often need three coats. A few reported peeling or damaged nails. Prep seems to matter a lot.

Essie Gel Couture is mainly loved for lasting a week to two weeks with a glossy, plump finish, easy application and fairly quick drying. The main downsides are shrinkage, especially in thick coats or as the bottle ages, plus thickness, sheer shades needing several coats, and for some nail damage or staining. A few see it chip early. Thin coats help.
